title: Virasoro Constraints for Projective Complete Intersections
main_claim: Every smooth complete intersection X in P^N satisfies the all-genus Virasoro constraints L_k Z_X = 0 (k >= -1), in every curve class and with arbitrary insertions, including primitive and odd ones. The proof is a double induction on dimension and on kappa = sum(d_i - 1). Factoring one equation gives a degeneration X ~> U ∪_D Bl_S M. The constraints are transported through capped chains: a switchwise inclusion-exclusion with relative caps built from HLR fiber invariants, and contractions done on the Steenbrink E1 page. The primitive part of the error is detected by a Hodge-Riemann Hermitian-norm test. Toric-bundle transfer (CGT) handles the ruled pieces and projective space.

issues.location: sections/evaluation.tex, Proposition ev:groups (Group product with retained evaluations)
issues.description: The disconnected product rule of AF2016 Prop. 4.14 is extended to groups of components that keep their joint aligned evaluations and are allowed to be disconnected. The proof relies on a cartesian square over a 'common refinement' expansion stack and a degree-one comparison, and is given only as a sketch. Everything else depends on this step: the idle-switch equality, and with it the whole sewing cancellation.
issues.evidence: 'The square ... is cartesian in the transverse expanded-map comparison' and 'Its degree-one virtual pushforward argument applied to (ev:group-square) proves (ev:group-vfc)'. The paper justifies this by analogy with AF2016 Lemmas 4.16-4.18 rather than by a complete argument.

issues.description: The lemma passes from Hodge-projector contractions on smooth fibers to Gr_F/Gr_W of the limiting MHS through canonical extensions. This silently needs every tensor in the diagram (GW correspondences, the inverse pairing) to be monodromy-invariant, i.e. compatible with N, and to be a filtered morphism of the extended bundles. That holds for the correspondences used here, but the paper does not state it.
issues.evidence: 'flat morphisms of variations extend as filtered morphisms. Their graded tensor contraction therefore extends with the same scalar value' — no hypothesis on unipotent monodromy compatibility is stated for the multivalued flat sections.

issues.description: CGT Theorem 1.4 is used for bases with odd and off-diagonal cohomology in the first-Hodge convention. The nu-intertwining (Hodge-difference equivariance of T and of I_as at tau_B=0) is argued only qualitatively, and so is the claim that the quantization scalar vanishes. Both are plausible but not checked in detail.
issues.evidence: 'every column of the base fundamental solution has the Hodge difference of its input ... Consequently nu_E T = T nu_col' — asserted, not computed.

coverage: Read: the introduction, conventions, detection and induction sections in full; the sewing section in full; the cap fiber block (linearization, finite spanning); the first-page pairing, first-index lemma, scalar-limit and chain-contraction lemmas; and the evaluation group-product proposition. Checked by hand: the vdim and output-codimension count r(e-e')+b in cap:linearization; the HLR scalar 1/(e^{r-j}((e-1)!)^r) (it reduces to 1/e! for (P^1, pt)), plus the jet Chern class and gerbe integral; the indexing of the Steenbrink E1 page for a family with no triple points; the central constant C_Y against the Chern-number formula (genus-g curve gives 0, P^2 gives -5/16); deriving L_0 from [L_1,L_{-1}] = 2L_0; the geometry of the splitting family (singular locus S, N_{S/M} = O(a)+O(d_r), dual seam normals O(b)|_D and O(-b)|_D, kappa decreasing); the codimension-2 blowup cohomology, nondegeneracy and primitivity of B0; the parity vanishing in the detection norm; local constancy of the Hermitian-square test (derivatives of the projectors are off-diagonal); the Noether-Lefschetz and very-general-fiber argument, including whether a very general X can be put in the pencil (it can, because f_r is free); and the trivial-monodromy argument for the exceptional surfaces. Not verified line by line: the full aligned-expansion restriction proposition in the evaluation section, the uniform bounds in the cap section, or Fujisawa's trace normalization.
